columns.rationale: null_rate is 0.0 across 45228 rows with 2330 distinct values and samples like '489434'-'489443' showing a dense numeric invoice identifier, so it is kept as-is and required.
null_rate is 0.0 with 3141 distinct alphanumeric codes (e.g. '10002R', '10123C'), so it stays VARCHAR and required; mixed alpha suffixes rule out an integer cast.
228 of 45228 rows are null (null_rate 0.005041) while samples show free-text product names, so the column is retained nullable rather than imputed.
All ten samples (-1395.0 .. -504.0) and the min/max of -1395.0/5184.0 are whole numbers landed as DECIMAL(38,9), so an INTEGER cast is supported; null_rate is 0.0.

Multiple sampled quantity values are negative (e.g. -1395.0, -1043.0, -1012.0), a pattern consistent with return/cancellation lines, so a boolean flag is derived as quantity < 0 rather than inferred from the invoice text, which the profile does not show with a cancellation prefix.
Every sample ('2009-12-01 07:45:00' through '2009-12-01 09:50:00') is an unambiguous ISO-shaped timestamp string with null_rate 0.0, so the VARCHAR is renamed to snake_case and cast to TIMESTAMP.
Samples range from 0.0 to 0.18 with two-decimal precision and max is 1998.49, min is 0.0, null_rate 0.0, so DECIMAL(10,2) fits the observed monetary values better than the landed DECIMAL(38,9).

Samples (12346.0, 12349.0, ...) are integral and min/max are 12346.0/18287.0, but null_rate is 0.29778 (13468 of 45228 rows), so the column is cast to INTEGER but kept nullable and sparsely populated rather than required.
null_rate is 0.0 with only 24 distinct values (e.g. 'Australia', 'Austria', 'Belgium'), consistent with a stable low-cardinality country field.
Flagged is_airbyte_metadata true; this is a capture-tool surrogate id with 45228 distinct UUID-like values, not a business column.
Flagged is_airbyte_metadata true with only 2 distinct extraction timestamps ('2026-07-27T10:24:46','...:47'); it records ingestion time, not business data.
Flagged is_airbyte_metadata true with a single constant distinct value '{}' across all rows, carrying no business information.

decisions.rationale: duplicate_row_rate is 0.011188 against row_count 45228 (about 506 duplicate rows), so fully identical rows are dropped before the silver table is built.

invoice (2330 distinct, null_rate 0.0) and stockcode (3141 distinct, null_rate 0.0) are the only two required, non-dropped columns that together plausibly identify one order line; no finer-grained line sequence column exists in the profile.

customer_id has null_rate 0.29778 (13468 of 45228 rows); nulls are retained rather than imputed or filtered, since the business meaning of a missing customer is a valid guest/anonymous transaction, not a build failure.
description has null_rate 0.005041 (228 of 45228 rows); the column is sparsely incomplete and is retained nullable rather than dropped or imputed.

_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are all flagged is_airbyte_metadata true and carry only ingestion-tool bookkeeping (UUIDs, a two-value extraction timestamp, and a constant empty JSON object), so none are proposed for silver.
All sampled quantity values are whole numbers (e.g. -1395.0, 5184.0 as max) landed as DECIMAL(38,9), so the column is cast to INTEGER.
price samples show at most two decimal places with max 1998.49 and min 0.0, so DECIMAL(10,2) is proposed instead of the landed DECIMAL(38,9).
invoicedate samples are uniformly ISO-shaped 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' strings with null_rate 0.0, supporting a TIMESTAMP cast and rename to invoice_date.
Negative quantity samples (e.g. -1395.0, -1043.0) indicate return or cancellation lines, so an is_return boolean is derived from quantity < 0 for consumer convenience.

purpose: This table provides a cleaned, line-item grain view of online retail transactions (invoice plus stock code) with typed dates, quantities, prices and customer identifiers, intended to feed sales, returns, and customer analytics.
usage: Consumers should treat each row as one invoice/stockcode line, use invoice_date as a TIMESTAMP for time-based analysis, filter or segment on is_return when excluding or isolating return/cancellation activity, and expect customer_id to be null for roughly 30% of rows representing transactions without an identified customer.
limitations: Exact duplicate rows (duplicate_row_rate 0.011188 of 45228 rows) are dropped but the invoice/stockcode grain is not guaranteed fully unique since repeated identical line entries within an invoice cannot be distinguished from the available columns; description is missing for 0.5% of rows and customer_id is missing for about 29.8% of rows, both retained as nulls rather than imputed.
